title: How a code walkthrough is created and shown
summary: The agent's `create_walkthrough` call is validated, stored per project, and then drawn by three independent UI pieces that only listen to the store.

steps.title: The agent calls `create_walkthrough`
steps.comment: The tool receives the whole walkthrough in **one call** and hands it to `Walkthrough::from_json`. It never edits a file: it only reads buffers and changes UI state, which is why it needs no permission prompt.

steps.title: Validation collects every problem
steps.comment: Errors are pushed onto the error list (highlighted) instead of returning early, so the agent can fix everything in a single retry. The step count and duplicate ids are checked before any file is opened.

steps.title: Errors go back to the agent together
steps.comment: On failure nothing is shown to the user. The tool result lists each problem on its own line, phrased so the model can act on it.

steps.title: Line numbers become anchors
steps.comment: The agent's 1-based line numbers are checked against the buffer as it is *now*. Further down, `anchor_text` rescues ranges that are off by a few lines, and the result is stored as anchors so it follows later edits.

steps.title: The store takes ownership
steps.comment: One store per project holds the active walkthrough. Setting it mints the id, activates the first step and emits `Created`. Every UI piece reacts to that event; none of them call each other.

steps.title: Editors annotate themselves
steps.comment: Each singleton editor has an addon subscribed to the store. On `Created` or `Dismissed` it first removes the blocks it added, then inserts a comment block below every step in its buffer. Nothing is written to the buffer.

steps.title: Navigation brings the step into view
steps.comment: A single subscriber opens the step's file in a code pane, puts the cursor at the start of the range without selecting it, and scrolls so the range comes first. Next, previous and flowchart clicks all end up here.

steps.title: The flowchart follows the active step
steps.comment: The view appends a `style` line for the active step's node and renders that source. Rendered diagrams are cached by source, so going back to a step is instant.

steps.title: Clicks map back to nodes
steps.comment: The diagram is painted as a bitmap, so a click is scaled from view coordinates into the SVG's coordinates and tested against the node rectangles read from the renderer's output.

flowchart:
flowchart TD
  tool[Agent calls create_walkthrough] --> validate{Input valid?}
  validate -- no --> errors[Return all errors to the agent]
  validate -- yes --> anchor[Resolve lines to anchors]
  anchor --> store[Store emits Created]
  store --> editor[Editors add highlights and comment blocks]
  store --> reveal[Navigation opens the step]
  store --> diagram[Flowchart view renders the diagram]
  diagram --> nodeclick[Node click picks a step]
  nodeclick --> reveal
